opening_message:
Ticket 1: Maurice Perez (employee ID E036) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E036.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Maurice Perez (E036) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access, and the role owns the system, so write is within policy. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check for Maurice Perez (E036): record shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training (never admin). The requested write access exceeds the maximum for a basic-trained contractor, so the maximum is read. Recommend granting read to Source Code.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR's note says full-time Engineer (which would allow write), while Security's note says contractor with basic security training (which caps at read, since contractors need advanced training for write and never admin). Because the employee's actual maximum per policy is at most read under the more restrictive Security record, and granting write could exceed policy, I grant the maximum allowable level: read. This level is within policy under both readings.
